section1.p:
The Polls XEP provides a framework for creating and managing polls within XMPP-based applications. Polls are a popular way to gather opinions, votes, or preferences from a group of users in real-time, and this XEP aims to standardize the process of initiating, participating in, and collecting results for polls in XMPP messaging environments.
By implementing this XEP, developers can easily integrate polling capabilities into their XMPP-based chat applications, allowing users to create polls with customizable options, cast votes, and view the results—either as they are updated in real time or after the poll has concluded.
The XEP outlines the structure of poll messages, including the creation of polls, the recording of votes, and the handling of results (both partial and final). Polls can be conducted in group chats, where participants send responses that are counted and processed automatically. The XEP also supports the broadcasting of poll results, ensuring that all participants stay informed on the voting progress.
This specification is ideal for collaborative environments where group decision-making is essential, such as organizing events, determining preferences, or gathering feedback from large communities.

section2.topic: Creating a poll in a group chat
section2.p: When a user creates a poll in a group chat, the client sends a <message> stanza containing a <poll> element. The poll includes a <description> element explaining the purpose of the poll, an <expiration> element indicating the deadline, and an <options> element listing the possible choices. Each option is represented by an <option> element with a unique 'id' attribute.

example.caption: User creates a poll in a group chat

section2.example: <message to="ismael.conference@ismael" id="message-4878787" type="groupchat"> <poll id="12345678" xmlns="urn:xmpp:poll:0"> <description> Poll to find out who can donate blood: </description> <expiration>2025-02-22T12:00:00Z</expiration> <!-- Poll expiration date --> <options> <option id="1">Of course, I'm in for the group donation on 02/22 :)</option> <option id="2">Of course, I'm in for 03/08 :)</option> <option id="3">I won't be able to this time :(</option> <option id="4">I'm in for 03/15 :)</option> <!-- New option added --> </options> </poll> </message>

section2.p: When a user votes in a poll, the client sends a <message> stanza containing a <poll> element. The poll is identified by its 'id' attribute, and the selected option is specified within an <option> element with a corresponding 'id'. This allows the server and other clients to register the user's vote properly.

example.caption: User votes for an option in the poll

section2.example: <message to="ismael.conference@ismael" id="message-4878788" type="groupchat"> <poll id="12345678" xmlns="urn:xmpp:poll:0"> <option id="1">Of course, I'm in for the group donation on 02/22 :)</option> </poll> </message>

section2.p: When a poll receives votes, the client sends a <message> stanza containing a <poll> element with a <result> sub-element. The 'final' attribute in the <result> element indicates whether the poll is still open ("false") or has ended ("true"). Each option in the poll is represented by an <option> element with an 'id' attribute and a 'votes' attribute, reflecting the current number of votes for that option. This message is sent every time a new vote is registered to keep participants updated.
section2.example: <message to="ismael.conference@ismael" id="message-4878790" type="groupchat"> <poll xmlns="urn:xmpp:poll:0" id="12345678"> <result final="false"> <option id="1" votes="3">Of course, I'm in for the group donation on 02/22 :)</option> <option id="2" votes="2">Of course, I'm in for 03/08 :)</option> <option id="3" votes="1">I won't be able to this time :(</option> </result> </poll> </message>
